cls: Antineoplastic - bispecific T-cell engager (CD20 x CD3)
pharm: Bispecific antibody binding CD20 x CD3; recruits cytotoxic T cells to tumour cells, triggering T-cell activation and tumour-cell lysis
tags: Boxed warning: neurologic toxicity including ICANS
REMS / step-up dosing with hospitalisation monitoring
quick: Step-up dosing then IV 30 mg every 3 weeks for up to 12 cycles (fixed duration); hospitalise/monitor for CRS around step-up doses
May cause fetal harm; effective contraception during and for months after last dose
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for months after last dose
No established adjustment; monitor CRS-related hypotension/AKI
CRS and ICANS signs, CBC, infection, HBV screen
summary: Glofitamab (Columvi) is a bispecific T-cell engager binding CD20 x CD3, indicated for Relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (including transformed) after at least 2 prior systemic lines. Treatment starts with step-up doses with CRS prophylaxis and close (often inpatient) monitoring, then continues at the full dose. Boxed warnings cover cytokine release syndrome and neurologic toxicity including ICANS.
indications: Relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (including transformed) after at least 2 prior systemic lines

dosage.d: Obinutuzumab pretreatment (debulking) then step-up 2.5 mg, 10 mg, then 30 mg (IV) per labeling
dosage.t: Premedicate (corticosteroid, antihistamine, antipyretic); monitor/hospitalise per labeling around each step-up dose

dosage.d: IV 30 mg every 3 weeks for up to 12 cycles (fixed duration)
dosage.t: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; hold for grade 3+ CRS/ICANS

admin: Give step-up doses exactly as labeled with premedications; observe for CRS/ICANS for the specified period
Have tocilizumab and corticosteroids available for CRS management
Do not drive or operate machinery during and after step-up and with neurotoxicity symptoms
Screen for infections including HBV before starting; hold for active infection
moa: One arm binds the tumour antigen and the other binds CD3 on T cells, forming an immune synapse that activates T cells to release perforin/granzymes and lyse tumour cells independent of MHC presentation.

relative: Severe CRS/ICANS on prior dose (rechallenge per grade-based rules)
Obinutuzumab pretreatment is mandatory to reduce CRS

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: No formal adjustment; CRS-related hypotension can precipitate AKI - monitor creatinine and volume status.
hepatic: No formal adjustment; monitor transaminases (CRS hepatitis overlap).

moderate: CYP substrates with narrow index during CRS (cytokine-mediated CYP suppression reverses with tocilizumab/corticosteroids)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; counsel on concomitant risks.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

emergency: Fever with low blood pressure or breathlessness after dosing (CRS) - seek emergency care
Confusion, difficulty writing/speaking, tremor or seizure (ICANS) - seek emergency care

monitoring: CRS/ICANS assessment around every step-up and early full doses
Infection surveillance; HBV serology at baseline
counsel: Fever, chills, dizziness, breathing difficulty or fast heartbeat after the injection can mean CRS - call immediately or go to emergency
Confusion, trouble finding words, shaking or seizure can mean brain toxicity - get help at once
Stay near the treating hospital during step-up doses as instructed; do not drive
Report any fever or infection signs promptly; avoid live vaccines
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed
pk: T-cell activation within hours of first step-up dose; CRS typically within days of step-up
Days (IgG-based bispecific); weekly to biweekly dosing
Refrigerate 2-8 C; do not freeze; use diluted solution promptly per labeling
pearls: Step-up dosing plus premedication is what makes outpatient continuation feasible - never skip it
CRS is treated with tocilizumab +/- corticosteroids; ICANS with corticosteroids (tocilizumab alone if isolated CRS)
Infection prophylaxis (including PJP/herpes) follows local protocol during lymphopenia
Fixed-duration (12 cycles) CD20 bispecific - treatment ends rather than continuing indefinitely
Obinutuzumab debulking distinguishes its CRS-mitigation strategy
missed: If a planned dose is missed, give it as soon as possible and adjust the schedule to maintain the planned interval; do not double the dose. Consult the full prescribing information for cycle-delay rules. Re-priming step-up is required after a prolonged gap - see labeling.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose is expected to exaggerate known toxicities (myelosuppression, GI effects, infusion reactions). Provide supportive care with close monitoring. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
